sn55.1:1.3: The legendary wheel-turning monarch, who ruled without violence from sea to sea, is depicted in detail in [dn17]() and [dn26]().
sn55.1:2.1: These are the four factors of stream-entry. The devotional passages that follow are regularly recited throughout Theravadin communities, and also form the basis of meditation on the triple gem.
sn55.1:2.3: _Bhagavā_ (“blessed one”, “lord”) is the normal honorific for the Buddha in Pali; in ordinary usage I translate it as “the Buddha”. The literal meaning is “one who has good fortune”, in which sense it stems from Vedic times (Rig Veda 7.41.5). In Pali it is used only for the Buddha, but elsewhere was a general honorific used, for example, by King Janaka to address Yajñavalkya (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.3.14), among respected peers (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 1.8.7), to a teacher (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.4.3), or by Manu to his daughter (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1.9).
